Save the Duckling — pygame game

Context

The user wants a game about a baby duckling searching for its mother, y C:\Users\cassandra\savetheduckling folder. Through clarifying questionswe settled on: a top-down maze/exploration game (single screen, no scrolling), where the challenge is collecting scattered sibling ducklings before reuniting with mother,
with simple sprite-image art. Since no image assets exist and we can't will be generated locally with Pillow (available: 12.2.0) as simple, cutePNGs, then loaded and rendered by pygame (available: 2.6.1) on Python 3.11.9.

File layout

savetheduckling/
├── main.py          # entry point: init, game loop, state machine, HU
├── constants.py     # tunable config: screen size, tile size, colors, speed, paths
├── assets_gen.py    # Pillow sprite/tile generator; regenerates asset
├── entities.py      # Player, Sibling, Mother, Obstacle sprite classes
├── level.py         # plain-Python level layout data + build_level()/
└── assets/          # generated PNGs (duckling, mother_duck, sibling_1-3, grass_tile,
                      #  water_tile, rock, bush)

Asset generation (assets_gen.py)

Runs before pygame.init() in main.py via ensure_assets() (cheap no-op pected files); also runnable standalone to regenerate art. Each sprite:Image.new("RGBA", (w,h), (0,0,0,0)) + ImageDraw shapes, saved as PNG, loaded later via pygame.image.load(path).convert_alpha(). TILE_SIZE = 40.

┌───────────────────┬───────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│       File        │ Size  │                         Construction
├───────────────────┼───────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ duckling.png      │ 32×32 │ yellow ellipse body + head, orange trian
├───────────────────┼───────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ mother_duck.png   │ 48×48 │ same recipe scaled up, cream body, extra
├───────────────────┼───────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ sibling_1/2/3.png │ 28×28 │ shared _draw_chick() helper, 3 slightly
├───────────────────┼───────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ grass_tile.png    │ 40×40 │ green fill + darker-green texture marks
├───────────────────┼───────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ water_tile.png    │ 40×40 │ blue fill + lighter wavy arcs (acts as a
├───────────────────┼───────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ rock.png          │ 40×40 │ jittered gray polygon + darker shading e
├───────────────────┼───────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ bush.png          │ 40×40 │ overlapping dark-green ellipses
└───────────────────┴───────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Game loop (main.py)

Two-state machine: GameState.PLAYING, GameState.WIN (simple Enum). Screen 960×640 (24×16 tiles) — exactly matches the level grid, so no camera/scrolling logic needed.

1. ensure_assets(), pygame.init(), create window/clock, load all images into a dict once.
2. level.build_level(images) → player, obstacles group, siblings groupbackground(images) → pre-tiled grass Surface blitted whole each frame.
3. Loop at 60 FPS: handle QUIT/ESC; while PLAYING — read input, player.update(dt, obstacles), spritecollide siblings (dokill=True, increments counter), check
   player.rect.colliderect(mother.rect) and collected >= TOTAL_SIBLING
4. Draw background, obstacles, mother, siblings, player, HUD text ("Siblings found: X/Y" + control hint). On WIN, overlay a dark translucent surface with centered "You found
   your family!" message.

Entities (entities.py)

- Obstacle, Sibling, Mother: simple pygame.sprite.Sprite with rect + i
- Player: float x,y position (frame-rate independent movement) synced to integer rect; handle_input() reads arrow keys + WASD, normalizes diagonal speed; update(dt,
  obstacles) resolves movement one axis at a time (move X → clamp to sacle collision; then same for Y), giving wall-sliding behavior with plainAABB rects — no physics engine, no pixel masks.

Level layout (level.py)

Plain Python grid data (col, row → pixels via TILE_SIZE): an OBSTACLE_LAYOUT list of ~12-18 (col,row,kind) tuples (rocks, bushes, and a small water-pond cluster) forming a
loose maze; SIBLING_SPAWNS list of 6 (col,row) points (sprite assigned PNGs); MOTHER_POS near the pond; PLAYER_START in the opposite corner.TOTAL_SIBLINGS = len(SIBLING_SPAWNS) is the single source of truth used for both the HUD and the win check. Outer map bounds are handled by clamping in Player.update, not by
border obstacle tiles.

Win condition

Mother is always reachable (no gating wall). Reaching her rect only trTOTAL_SIBLINGS; reaching her early just does nothing mechanically (HUDalready shows the shortfall). Keeps the logic to one conditional instead of adding a second "gate" entity.

Scope

Single screen (no scrolling/camera), 6 siblings, ~12-18 static obstacle tiles, AABB rect collision only, no audio, no menu beyond PLAYING/WIN — matches the user's "top-down
maze," "collect siblings," and "keep it simple" choices.

Verification

- Run python assets_gen.py standalone first and open a couple of genery look reasonable before wiring up pygame.
- Run python main.py, confirm the window opens at 960×640, duckling moves smoothly with arrows/WASD, stops at obstacles/screen edges (with sliding along walls), sibling
  sprites disappear and the HUD counter increments on contact, and reag all 6 does nothing while reaching her after collecting all 6 shows thewin overlay.
- Confirm ESC and window-close both quit cleanly at any state.

  import main, pygame
  import constants, level

  main.ensure_assets()
  pygame.init()
  screen = pygame.display.set_mode((constants.SCREEN_WIDTH, constants.SCREEN_HEIGHT))
  images = main.load_images()
  background = level.build_background(images)
  player, obstacles, siblings, mother = level.build_level(images)
  print('player start', player.rect)
  print('mother', mother.rect)
  print('num obstacles', len(obstacles))
  print('num siblings', len(siblings))

  # simulate moving right for a bit
  for i in range(120):
      player.dx, player.dy = 1, 0
      player.update(1/60, obstacles)
  print('player after moving right:', player.rect)

  # simulate collecting all siblings by teleporting player onto them
  collected = 0
  for s in list(siblings):
      player.rect.topleft = s.rect.topleft
      hits = pygame.sprite.spritecollide(player, siblings, dokill=True)
      collected += len(hits)
  print('collected', collected, 'total', level.TOTAL_SIBLINGS)

  player.rect.topleft = mother.rect.topleft
  win = player.rect.colliderect(mother.rect) and collected >= level.TOTAL_SIBLINGS
  print('win condition met:', win)
  pygame.quit()
  print('OK')

● Bash(cd "C:\Users\cassandra\savetheduckling" && SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy pyt
  import pygame, main, level, constants
  main.ensure_assets()
  pygame.init()
  screen = pygame.display.set_mode((constants.SCREEN_WIDTH, constants.SCREE
  images = main.load_images()
  background = level.build_background(images)
  player, obstacles, siblings, mother = level.build_level(images)
  screen.blit(background, (0,0))
  obstacles.draw(screen)
  screen.blit(mother.image, mother.rect)
  siblings.draw(screen)
  screen.blit(player.image, player.rect)
  font = pygame.font.SysFont(None, 28)
  screen.blit(font.render(f'Siblings found: 0/{level.TOTAL_SIBLINGS}', True0))
  pygame.image.save(screen, 'screenshot.png')
  pygame.quit()
  print('saved')

The game is complete and working in C:\Users\cassandra\savetheduckling:

- python main.py to play — a 960×640 window opens with your duckling in t
- Move with arrow keys or WASD, navigate around rocks/bushes/water, and collect all 6 sibling ducklings scattered across the map.
- A HUD in the top-left tracks Siblings found: X/6. Once all 6 are collec the pond (bottom-right) to trigger the "You found your family!" winscreen.
- ESC or closing the window quits at any time.

All sprites (duckling, mother, siblings, grass, water, rocks, bushes) wers_gen.py using Pillow — no external assets needed. Re-run pythonassets_gen.py anytime to regenerate/tweak the art.
